modules.name: Site wind climate and reference wind statistics
modules.effort: S: 4-5 person-days (ECCC/EPW parsing, averaging-time and exposure transfer, ReferenceSpec, wind rose, data-quality badge)
modules.design_question: Which wind directions and speeds, by season and hour of use, drive pedestrian wind at this site, at what stated reference, and are the source data adequate?
inputs: Layer 0 georeference and true-north offset (VTC site-plan north arrow is rotated relative to the street grid)
Hourly station record (speed, direction, temperature, humidity), 30 years or more, e.g. ECCC Vancouver Intl A or Vancouver Harbour CS, or NOAA ISD; station gust kept for QA only
EPW/TMYx file for solar and the typical-year time base (feeds M06)
Station metadata: anemometer height, observation averaging period (1, 2 or 10 min), terrain roughness at the station
Site terrain roughness and displacement (user choice, logged)
outputs: WindClimate: hourly series (speed, direction, season tag, comfort-hour flag, concurrent temperature and humidity) carrying a ReferenceSpec
ReferenceSpec: reference height z_ref, roughness length z0, profile law, averaging time, direction reference (true north), transfer model and version
WindRoseTable: 16 sectors x speed bins x season
NorthOffset (degrees)
DataQualityBadge (record length, completeness, exposure mismatch, averaging-time conversion declared)

parameters.name: Hourly wind record length
parameters.relationship: Longer record (30 years minimum in Toronto and Hamilton; RWDI's Cambridge example used 20) -> steadier frequencies of rare events such as the 0.1% safety gust (about 9 h/yr) -> more reliable pass/fail. Sensitivity itself is not quantified.

parameters.name: Comfort hours and season split
parameters.relationship: Comfort uses 06:00-23:00 winds, safety 24 h. Toronto reports four seasons, Hamilton and RWDI two, City of London a worst-season view plus June-August; fewer seasons hide storm-season exceedances that an annual average smooths out.

parameters.name: Station-to-site exposure correction
parameters.relationship: Station speeds are corrected for terrain and scaled through gradient height (Toronto example 600 m) to the site. Skipping this biases every downstream exceedance; direction and size of the bias depend on site roughness and are not quantified here.

parameters.name: Reference height and roughness (ReferenceSpec)
parameters.relationship: Speed depends on the height at which it is quoted: City of London scale factors run from 0.96 (100 m) to 1.48 (600 m) for one climate. A reference mismatch with the VAF scales every probe speed and shifts comfort classes.

parameters.name: Observation averaging time
parameters.relationship: ECCC speeds are 1-, 2- or 10-minute means ending at the observation; shorter means read higher than hourly means, so unconverted data inflate exceedances. No sourced conversion factor found; the choice is logged.

parameters.name: True-north offset of the site plan
parameters.relationship: ECCC directions are true north, so only the site-plan rotation needs correcting. A wrong offset assigns wind to the wrong facade by the same angle, shifting where downwash and corner flows are predicted.

parameters.name: Time-base concurrency
parameters.relationship: Temperature, humidity and wind from the same hours of one record keep cold-and-windy events together for M06; mixing a typical-year file with a 30-year wind record scrambles them. Logical rule, no source.

metrics.name: Hourly record length
metrics.good: >= 30 years of hourly data
metrics.bad: < 30 years
metrics.method: Count years with adequate hourly coverage
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR 6.4.4 and Hamilton 2026 both specify at least 30 years of hourly data; the RWDI Cambridge report used 1995-2015, so 30 years is a municipal rule, not universal

metrics.name: Season and hour convention declared
metrics.good: Declared set: Toronto four seasons; Hamilton and RWDI two (May-Oct, Nov-Apr); City of London worst season plus Jun-Aug; comfort 06:00-23:00 where stated, safety 24 h
metrics.bad: Annual-only or all-hours comfort statistics
metrics.method: Check run configuration against the selected CriteriaSet
metrics.basis: Toronto 5.3 and 6.4.4; Hamilton technical requirement 3; RWDI Cambridge report; City of London results section

metrics.name: ReferenceSpec completeness
metrics.good: z_ref, z0, profile law, averaging time and direction reference all declared; transfer model logged
metrics.bad: Any field missing, or station speed used as site speed
metrics.method: Schema check on WindClimate before it is released to M03-M06
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.4 requires terrain-corrected data scaled to gradient height; City of London requires a stated reference height and a location unaffected by the models

metrics.name: Averaging-time conversion
metrics.good: Station period (1, 2 or 10 min) converted to the criteria averaging time with a logged factor
metrics.bad: Raw station speeds treated as hourly means
metrics.method: Read the averaging period from station metadata; apply and log a conversion
metrics.basis: ECCC glossary states the 1-, 2- or 10-minute period; no sourced conversion factor found

metrics.name: Station representativeness
metrics.good: Station exposure and airshed comparable to the downtown site, with documented correction
metrics.bad: Uncorrected airport data used as site wind
metrics.method: Compare station and site roughness and distance; log the correction model; cross-check against a nearer station when one exists
metrics.basis: No sourced numeric distance or exposure limit; ECCC lists Vancouver Harbour CS (hourly year options 1976-2026) beside Vancouver Intl A, but anemometer exposure and wind coverage are not verified

metrics.name: Concurrent time base
metrics.good: Temperature, humidity and wind from the same record hours, or all variables from one TMYx year
metrics.bad: Typical-year temperature with a 30-year wind record
metrics.method: Tag each series with its record id and years; refuse to merge series with different ids
metrics.basis: Design rule for M06; no external source

modules.method: 1) Read the 30-year hourly station record (speed, direction, temperature, humidity) and the EPW/TMYx for solar. 2) Take direction as true north (ECCC convention) and rotate by the Layer 0 offset. 3) Convert the station averaging period to the criteria averaging time with a logged factor (team choice). 4) Apply an exposure correction: station terrain to gradient height to the site, with a named model (Toronto: established mathematical models; City of London: ESDU 01008), and write the result as a ReferenceSpec. 5) Bin into 16 sectors of 22.5 degrees, speed classes and seasons, for comfort hours (06:00-23:00) and safety hours (24 h). 6) Emit WindClimate with concurrent temperature and humidity, the ReferenceSpec and a data-quality badge. Station gust is kept for QA only. 7) Rank seasons from the data to find the governing season.
visualization: Polar wind rose per season (16 sectors, stacked speed bins in km/h), one panel per season, with the true-north arrow and the rotated street-grid axis overlaid
Bar chart of hours per sector above 20 km/h (corrected reference speed) per season, with a season-ranking table computed from the data
Data-quality badge (green/amber/red) with a ReferenceSpec card (z_ref, z0, averaging time, transfer model) linking to the Toronto and City of London clauses

modules.limits: TMY/EPW files are constructed typical years, not 30-year hourly records, so rare storms are under-represented. Airport anemometers differ from downtown exposure beside Burrard Inlet; ECCC speeds are 1-10 minute means and station gusts are sparse peaks. Pedestrian statistics (frequent winds) are not the 1-in-50-year design wind used in P10. The climate is treated as stationary; no future weather files are applied.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the station and correction model, deciding whether site-specific data or a consultant study is needed, and interpreting local Vancouver flows such as winter outflow and storm winds.

modules.name: Wind-study requirement and criteria selector
modules.effort: S: 3-4 person-days (rule tables, five versioned CriteriaSets, clause-linked report)
modules.design_question: Will this massing probably need a formal pedestrian wind study in Vancouver, and which comfort and safety criteria set, with its own safety limit, should the tool apply and cite?
inputs: Layer 0: maximum tower height, count of buildings at or above 20 m, site area
Context building heights from the SITE module, including approved and future towers named in the VTC brief
Program tags: entrances, seating, transit plaza, amenity terraces
User choice of criteria family and trigger preset
outputs: StudyTriggerReport (per analog jurisdiction: Toronto 2022, Hamilton 2026, City of London 2019; clause links and document status)

CriteriaSet: versioned typed JSON (family and version, classes, speeds and units, exceedance basis, averaging as mean or GEM, comfort hours, seasons, zone-to-class map, mandatory safety criterion or explicit none, source id, status) consumed by M04 and M06
ScenarioChecklist (existing / proposed / proposed plus approved towers / mitigation / phasing)
ContextSpec: minimum context radius and cumulative tower list for M05

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: Taller tower -> higher trigger level and a tunnel requirement: Toronto Area 1 over 100 m is High, Hamilton 44 m or more, City of London above 100 m needs tunnel and CFD at detailed design. VTC towers of 244-305 m exceed every analog threshold found.

parameters.name: Height relative to surrounding buildings
parameters.relationship: Hamilton requires a tunnel study when a building of 20 m or more exceeds twice its surroundings; City of London steps up to CFD and tunnel at up to 4 times average surrounding height. Taller relative to context -> stricter study.

parameters.name: Number of buildings of 20 m or more
parameters.relationship: Two or more tall buildings move Toronto projects up one trigger level and trigger a tunnel study in Hamilton; multi-tower schemes therefore face stricter study types.

parameters.name: Criteria family and exceedance basis
parameters.relationship: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI limit GEM at 20% exceedance; City Lawson limits mean and GEM at 5%. Safety differs too: 90 km/h at 0.1% against 15 m/s at 0.022%. One family per run, never mixed.

parameters.name: Modelled context radius and cumulative scenario
parameters.relationship: Toronto asks about 350 m, Hamilton and City of London 400 m, plus influential taller buildings beyond. Larger radius and inclusion of approved towers -> truer approach flow and sheltering; the VTC brief names approved towers, so the cumulative case is required.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion
parameters.relationship: Policy criterion says a higher building should not contribute to adverse microclimate effects; it has no number, so the team must adopt numeric criteria and state why. Wording seen only in search snippets of the 2011/2018 versions.

metrics.name: Toronto-analog trigger level (downtown Area 1)
metrics.good: Low: over 20 m and under 60 m (CFD Phase 1 and 2 only)
metrics.bad: High: over 100 m (CFD Phase 1 plus wind-tunnel study at rezoning)
metrics.method: Compare tower height and context with Toronto Table 1 and the 3.b shift rules
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR Tables 1 and 2, re-read in r1

metrics.name: Hamilton-analog trigger
metrics.good: Under 20 m: no study
metrics.bad: 44 m or more, or 20 m+ and over 2x surroundings, or 2+ buildings of 20 m+: quantitative wind-tunnel study
metrics.method: Evaluate Hamilton rules 1-3 on Layer 0
metrics.basis: Hamilton guidelines, last updated 20 Feb 2026; adoption status unconfirmed (file name says 'ph1proposed')

metrics.name: City of London-analog trigger
metrics.good: Similar to or lower than surroundings and up to 25 m: no study unless sensitive uses
metrics.bad: Above 100 m: tunnel or CFD for massing, then tunnel and CFD by independent consultants at detailed design
metrics.method: Compare height and average surrounding height with the City of London approach table
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 table of recommended approach by building height

metrics.name: Vancouver Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion
metrics.good: No adverse microclimate effects (qualitative)
metrics.bad: Adverse microclimate effects
metrics.method: Present as qualitative pass/flag linked to the chosen numeric criteria in M04
metrics.basis: 2011/2018 policy wording seen only in search snippets; 1997 PDF not opened; the Shape Your City copy returned only a download page

metrics.name: Default criteria set for Vancouver runs
metrics.good: Toronto 2022 three-class set (10/15/20 km/h GEM at 80%), editable; Hamilton 2026 is equal or stricter at every shared class
metrics.bad: Unstated or mixed criteria
metrics.method: Preset selection stored with the run and shown in every result
metrics.basis: No Vancouver numeric criteria found. Toronto chosen as the downtown tall-building analog with an explicit High tier, a verified zone-to-class table and three classes; Hamilton, RWDI mph and City Lawson selectable

metrics.name: CriteriaSet integrity
metrics.good: Each set carries its own classes, exceedance basis, averaging and safety criterion (Toronto 10/15/20 km/h; Hamilton 10/14/17/20; RWDI 6/8/10/12 mph; City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s)
metrics.bad: A merged 'RWDI/Toronto' set, Lawson speeds at 20%, or a set with no safety criterion
metrics.method: Schema validation of each CriteriaSet at load and at run
metrics.basis: Earlier spec merged Toronto's three classes with the four classes of RWDI and Hamilton; corrected after the round-1 critique

metrics.name: Context radius and scenario set
metrics.good: Radius at least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond; scenarios existing, proposed, proposed plus approved and future towers, mitigation, phasing
metrics.bad: 350 m radius, or no cumulative scenario
metrics.method: Check ContextSpec against the run; list towers added beyond the radius
metrics.basis: 350 m (Toronto) and 400 m (Hamilton, City of London) are minima with taller buildings beyond to be included; the 2H term is a team assumption

modules.method: Read maximum tower height, count of buildings of 20 m or more, site area and context heights from Layer 0 and the SITE module. Evaluate each analog rule set (Toronto Table 1 with +1 level shifts, Hamilton rules 1-3, City of London height bands, Barrie 6-storey trigger) and output a level per jurisdiction with clause link and document status. Load the chosen CriteriaSet: classes, speeds and units, exceedance, averaging (mean or GEM), hours, seasons, zone map, safety criterion, source id, status. A set with no safety criterion is flagged and blocks safety output. Custom edits become team assumptions; claims later found wrong stay visible as FALSE ASSUMPTION. Emit ContextSpec (radius of at least max(400 m, about 2H), cumulative towers) and the scenario checklist (16 CFD or 36 tunnel directions).
visualization: Summary card with four chips (Toronto-analog, Hamilton-analog, City of London-analog, Vancouver policy) coloured pass/flag, each linking to the clause and showing document status

Grouped bar chart of comfort thresholds in km/h per category for Toronto, Hamilton, RWDI (mph converted) and City Lawson (m/s converted, hatched because the basis is 5% exceedance on mean and GEM), with a side table of each safety criterion
Checklist of required evidence items with ticks, including context radius and cumulative scenario

libraries.role: Validate CriteriaSet records (licence not re-verified)

modules.limits: No City of Vancouver numeric wind criteria or mandatory trigger could be found; vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, bylaws and council domains returned HTTP 403, so absence is not proven. Presets are Ontario, RWDI and City of London practice, not Vancouver law. The brief is an academic exercise and its jury may reward justified breaches.
modules.human_judgment: Which criteria family to adopt, how to argue any breach to the jury, and confirming with the City Rezoning Centre what a real application would need.

modules.name: Early massing wind-risk screening
modules.effort: M: 7-10 person-days (geometry rules, 3D flag overlay, source-linked reasons)
modules.design_question: Which massing moves (tower height, podium, step-backs, corners, tower gaps, through-block openings) are likely to create downwash, corner acceleration or channelling in the public realm?
inputs: Layer 0 footprints, heights, canopy objects and program tags
Context building heights within the ContextSpec radius from M02 (default max(400 m, about 2H))
WindClimate from M01 (prevailing and strong-wind sectors)
Zone tags: entrances, sidewalks, plazas, transit plaza, mid-block connections
outputs: WindRiskField: Low/Medium/High per facade segment, corner and public-space zone, with reason codes and clause links
RankedActions list (largest-scale changes first)
DirectionalExposure table (windward width and exposure height by sector)
PriorityProbes: probe points to seed M04 and M05
CanopyCoverageTable per frontage (to M06)

parameters.name: Exposure height above upwind context
parameters.relationship: Tower height above the tallest upwind context (sector-weighted) -> more stream intercepted and redirected downward (downwash) onto the base; short buildings rarely cause adverse impacts. Regulatory ratio triggers such as Hamilton's 2x sit in M02.

parameters.name: Windward facade width
parameters.relationship: Wider windward face -> larger intercepted flow and stronger downwash; Hamilton states tall, wide facades are generally undesirable.

parameters.name: Podium and tower offset from podium edge
parameters.relationship: Podium with a set-back tower deflects downflow before it reaches the street, lowering pedestrian-level speed; Toronto lists tower offset change as a significant wind change. Size of the benefit is not quantified in sources.

parameters.name: Lower building directly upwind of the tower
parameters.relationship: A lower upwind building can enlarge downflow on the tower and accelerate wind in the gap and at windward corners, yet shorter buildings upwind of taller ones lower tower exposure. Net effect depends on gap and heights.

parameters.name: Corner geometry
parameters.relationship: Sharp corners -> flow separates and accelerates at pedestrian level; chamfered or rounded corners streamline flow, stepped or re-entrant corners diffuse it, lowering corner speeds.

parameters.name: Gap between buildings aligned with strong-wind sector
parameters.relationship: Narrow gaps aligned with the wind channel and accelerate flow; wider spacing eases it. In idealised canyon runs a gap of 2x height gave larger uncomfortable zones than 1x, so the effect is not monotonic.

parameters.name: Through-block openings, underpasses, colonnades
parameters.relationship: Passages and underpasses force flow through a narrow section -> acceleration along mid-block connections; colonnades and arcades are also listed as large-scale wind-control features, so effect depends on orientation.

parameters.name: Canopies, recessed entrances, covered walkways
parameters.relationship: Deep, wrap-around and corner canopies and recessed entrances intercept downwash and create sheltered waiting zones; effect is local and secondary to massing. Canopy coverage also feeds rain protection in M06.

metrics.name: Exposure height above upwind context
metrics.good: Lower than the baseline scheme in the strongest-wind sectors
metrics.bad: Higher than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Tower top minus the highest upwind roof within the radius, weighted by sector frequency from M01
metrics.basis: Discriminates between options (the regulatory height triggers now sit in M02 because every VTC scheme is High); no sourced limit

metrics.name: Windward facade width by sector
metrics.good: Narrower than the baseline scheme toward strong-wind sectors
metrics.bad: Wide face toward a strong-wind sector
metrics.method: Projected facade width perpendicular to each 22.5 degree sector
metrics.basis: Direction sourced (Hamilton: tall and wide facades are generally undesirable); no numeric limit

metrics.name: Windward corner treatment
metrics.good: Chamfered, rounded, stepped or re-entrant corners
metrics.bad: Sharp corners on a tall windward volume
metrics.method: Detect corner turning angle and tag treatment
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.7.2 building-form strategies (qualitative)

metrics.name: Tower-podium offset depth
metrics.good: No sourced target; calibrate with M05 runs
metrics.bad: No sourced limit
metrics.method: Measure tower face to podium edge
metrics.basis: Direction of effect sourced, magnitude not

metrics.name: Lower building within one tower height upwind
metrics.good: None within one tower height in a strong-wind sector
metrics.bad: Present within one tower height
metrics.method: Distance from tower to lower upwind buildings along each strong-wind sector
metrics.basis: Mechanism sourced (Toronto, Hamilton); the one-tower-height distance is an editable placeholder

metrics.name: Gap aligned with strong-wind sector
metrics.good: Not aligned (outside one 22.5 degree sector)
metrics.bad: Aligned within one 22.5 degree sector of a strong-wind direction
metrics.method: Gap axis angle vs sector with strong-wind frequency from M01
metrics.basis: Editable placeholder; mechanism sourced, angle not

metrics.name: Composite wind-risk index per facade, corner and zone
metrics.good: Low band (editable cut-off)
metrics.bad: High band (editable cut-off)
metrics.method: Weighted sum of rule flags by sector frequency; weights and cut-offs are team assumptions to be recalibrated against CFD
metrics.basis: No sourced scoring scheme exists

modules.method: For each of 16 wind sectors, weighted by seasonal strong-wind frequency from M01: (1) compute each tower's exposure height above the upwind context within the M02 radius and its windward width; (2) detect lower buildings within one tower height upwind (team assumption); (3) find gaps and passages whose axis lies within one sector of the wind; (4) flag windward corners by turning angle and treatment (sharp, chamfer, round, step); (5) check podium offset and canopy presence at entrance and sidewalk zones. Each rule gives Low/Medium/High and a reason code with clause link. Flags combine into an editable 0-100 index per facade segment, corner and zone (weights are team assumptions). Regulatory height triggers sit in M02. Output priority probes for M04/M05 and a canopy-coverage table for M06.
visualization: Plan view of Layer 0 with arrows per strong-wind sector; windward corners as dots and facade segments as lines coloured Low (blue) / Medium (amber) / High (red)
Ground-plane zone polygons shaded by index with a 0-100 legend
Radar chart of the eight factors per tower
Reason-code table; each row links to the Toronto/Hamilton/RWDI clause, with a banner stating that this is screening and predicts no speeds

modules.limits: Rule-based screening ranks risk; it does not predict speeds or class compliance. Interaction of several towers, supertall scale (over 244 m), complex context and topography break simple rules. Use it to compare options and place CFD probes. Numeric rule cut-offs, including the one-tower-height upwind distance, are unsourced and editable.
modules.human_judgment: Weighing wind against daylight, program, structure and 'City in Nature' placemaking, and deciding how much residual risk the scheme accepts.

modules.name: Pedestrian wind comfort and safety classifier
modules.effort: M: 6-8 person-days in total; core subset (typed VAF import with reference gate, probe-hour engine, season classes, zone pass/fail, indicative safety) about 4-5 days; delta and low-wind maps follow in v1
modules.design_question: Given directional amplification factors at probes on a stated reference, what comfort class and safety status result per season, and do entrances, sidewalks, plazas and terraces meet their intended use?
inputs: WindClimate and ReferenceSpec from M01
VAFField with its own ReferenceSpec: from M05, or a typed CSV import (Eddy3D, wind-tunnel or consultant data) checked against an import template; M05 is optional
ProbeSet with zone tags from Layer 0 (entrance, sidewalk, seating, transit plaza, terrace)
CriteriaSet from M02 (with its safety criterion)
Optional turbulent kinetic energy or gust factor per probe
outputs: ReferenceGateReport: pass, or refusal with the mismatched fields, or the logged conversion applied
ComfortMap: per probe and season, exceedance fraction, class, pass/fail against the zone requirement
SafetyFlags (indicative below L3; blocked when the CriteriaSet has no safety criterion)
ZoneComplianceTable
ProbeWindSeries: hourly mean and GEM series at the probe, with time base and ReferenceSpec, for M06

parameters.name: Reference chain (U_ref and VAF normalisation)
parameters.relationship: V_p = VAF x U_ref needs U_ref at the height, roughness and profile law that normalised the VAF. Eddy3D ABL defaults (10 m, z0 1 m) and City of London (above 100 m) differ; a mismatch scales every probe speed and moves classes.

parameters.name: Criteria family and exceedance basis
parameters.relationship: Lower allowed exceedance (City Lawson 5% against Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI 20%) -> stricter class for the same wind; speed limits are used only with their own exceedance basis, averaging and safety criterion.

parameters.name: Gust treatment
parameters.relationship: GEM is the larger of mean speed and gust divided by 1.85, gust being mean plus 3 RMS; higher turbulence -> higher GEM -> worse class at the same mean. City Lawson uses mean and GEM and takes the worse; the Hagbo version uses mean only.

parameters.name: Zone to required class
parameters.relationship: Toronto: Sitting for seating, balconies and terraces; Standing for entrances and bus stops; Walking for sidewalks and laneways. RWDI: walking or strolling suits sidewalks. Stricter intended use -> lower tolerable speed -> more failures.

parameters.name: Number of simulated wind directions
parameters.relationship: Fewer directions -> coarser, less reliable class map. In one case 16 directions reproduced the 64-direction class over 96% of the area, 8 over 92%, 4 over 79%; City of London requires 36.

parameters.name: Season and governing season
parameters.relationship: The worst season sets the verdict, but which season governs Vancouver must be read from the M01 wind rose; Ontario statements about winter and spring do not transfer. Hamilton accepts some winter degradation as outdoor use falls.

parameters.name: Probe density and placement
parameters.relationship: Sparser probes can miss corner and entrance hot spots; Toronto and Hamilton expect probes about every 10 m along frontages and at least about 50 locations; City of London asks for about 3 probes at each corner.

metrics.name: Reference-chain gate
metrics.good: VAF reference equals the U_ref reference, or a logged conversion is applied
metrics.bad: Mismatched or missing reference: classification refused
metrics.method: Compare ReferenceSpec fields (z_ref, z0, profile law, averaging time, probe height)
metrics.basis: City of London: reference at a height and location unaffected by the models, with scale factors 0.96-1.48; Toronto 6.4.4: terrain-corrected, gradient-height-scaled data

metrics.name: Empty-domain unit test
metrics.good: Probe without buildings reproduces the undisturbed profile speed at probe height within 5%
metrics.bad: Deviation above 5%
metrics.method: Run the import or M05 with no buildings and compare with the profile from the ReferenceSpec
metrics.basis: Test design; the 5% tolerance is an editable placeholder

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (Toronto 2022, three classes)
metrics.good: GEM at or below the zone limit for at least 80% of 06:00-23:00 hours: Sitting 10, Standing 15, Walking 20 km/h
metrics.bad: GEM above 20 km/h for more than 20% of hours (Uncomfortable), or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: Exceedance of the hourly GEM series per season (four seasons)
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR Table 3; earlier label 'RWDI/Toronto' merged two different sets and is corrected

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (Hamilton 2026, four classes)
metrics.good: Sitting under 10, Standing under 14, Strolling under 17, Walking under 20 km/h at 80% occurrence, two seasons (May-Oct, Nov-Apr)
metrics.bad: Over 20 km/h (Uncomfortable)
metrics.method: As above with Hamilton limits and two seasons
metrics.basis: Hamilton Table 1, last updated 20 Feb 2026

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (RWDI, mph)
metrics.good: GEM at or below 6 (Sitting), 8 (Standing), 10 (Strolling), 12 mph (Walking), i.e. about 9.7/12.9/16.1/19.3 km/h, at 20% exceedance, 06:00-23:00
metrics.bad: Above 12 mph (Uncomfortable) or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: As above with RWDI limits; summer May-Oct, winter Nov-Apr
metrics.basis: RWDI Cambridge report criteria table; not identical to Hamilton's 14 and 17 km/h

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (City Lawson, London 2019)
metrics.good: Mean and GEM at or below 2.5 (Frequent Sitting), 4 (Occasional Sitting), 6 (Standing), 8 m/s (Walking) for 95% of comfort hours; the worse of mean and GEM governs
metrics.bad: Above 8 m/s (Uncomfortable) or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: Exceedance at the 5% level on both series; worst season plus June-August
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 guideline, a modified Lawson LDDC set

metrics.name: Lawson, Hagbo 2022 version (mean speed only)
metrics.good: Mean speed at or below 4 (Sitting), 6 (Standing), 8 (Strolling), 10 m/s (Business walking) for at most 5% of hours; comfort only
metrics.bad: Safety reported from this set, or described as a GEM set
metrics.method: Exceedance at the 5% level on mean speed
metrics.basis: Secondary source: 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, no safety criterion; primary Lawson text not opened

metrics.name: Safety criterion bound to the family
metrics.good: Gust over 90 km/h for no more than 0.1% of 24 h hours (about 9 h/yr) for Toronto, Hamilton, RWDI (56 mph); City Lawson 15 m/s mean and GEM at 0.022% (about 2 h/yr)
metrics.bad: Toronto safety applied to a Lawson run, or a set with no safety limit reporting safety
metrics.method: Read the safety field of the CriteriaSet; compute the annual exceedance on 24 h hours
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3, Hamilton Table 2, RWDI 56 mph, City of London safety table

metrics.name: Low-wind flag
metrics.good: GEM under 5 km/h for less than 80% of hours
metrics.bad: GEM under 5 km/h for 80% or more: low air circulation, possible exhaust build-up and heat in full sun
metrics.method: Share of hours below 5 km/h
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3 note 3

metrics.name: Significance of change against baseline
metrics.good: Negligible or beneficial: class unchanged or calmer
metrics.bad: Major adverse: safe becomes unsafe, or suitable becomes unsuitable
metrics.method: Delta of class per probe, existing vs proposed, rated with the City of London scheme
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 significance tables; Hamilton: improve where possible, no significant degradation, winter allowance

metrics.name: Sidewalk required class
metrics.good: Walking at least; Strolling preferred where the set has it
metrics.bad: Uncomfortable on a sidewalk, or Sitting demanded of all sidewalks
metrics.method: Zone map in the CriteriaSet

modules.method: Gate: stop if the VAFField ReferenceSpec differs from the WindClimate one, unless a logged transfer applies. For each probe p and hour h: V_p(h) = VAF_p(theta_h) x U_ref(h), interpolating between the two nearest simulated directions (Eddy3D offers Interpolate or Nearest). Gust from mean + 3 x RMS, or from turbulent kinetic energy when supplied (Eddy3D: U + g x sqrt(2k/3)). GEM = max(mean, gust/1.85) for GEM families; mean-only and mean-and-GEM rules follow the family. Per season, take the best class whose exceedance fraction over comfort hours is within the family's allowance (20% or 5%). Safety: share of 24 h hours above the family's limit; no safety criterion means no safety output. Compare with the zone requirement, flag low-wind probes, rate change against the existing scenario.
visualization: Four false-colour maps (one per season) on the ground plane at 1.5 m: Sitting, Standing, Walking, Uncomfortable in a colour-blind-safe sequential ramp, plus Strolling or the two Lawson sitting classes when those sets are chosen
Black hatched markers for probes violating the safety criterion, labelled indicative below L3
Per-zone pass/fail badges (entrance, sidewalk, plaza, terrace) linked to the clause that sets the limit, and a reference-chain badge (z_ref, z0, averaging time)

Existing-vs-proposed delta map rated with the City of London significance scheme, and a probe table with GEM, exceedance and class; banner 'No VAFField imported: M03 screening only' when no data are loaded

Approved and future towers as a required cumulative context scenario, plus influential taller towers beyond the radius when upwind

parameters.name: Proximity model radius
parameters.relationship: Toronto asks about 350 m, Hamilton and City of London 400 m, plus influential taller buildings beyond. That is only about 1.1-1.6 tower heights for 244-305 m towers; a larger radius capturing upwind towers -> truer approach flow and wakes.

parameters.name: Domain size relative to H
parameters.relationship: Top, lateral and outlet distances scale with the tallest building. The Hagbo and Giljarhus run used height 6 H and outlet and lateral 15 H, citing 5 H above the tallest building; smaller domains raise blockage, so it is logged. COST 732 and AIJ limits not opened.

parameters.name: Number of wind directions
parameters.relationship: Toronto requires at least 16 for CFD and 36 for tunnel; City of London 36 for all studies; Hamilton CFD may use prevailing directions only, weighted over all directions. Fewer directions -> coarser classes (79% same class with 4, 96% with 16, by area, one case).

parameters.name: Turbulence model and steadiness
parameters.relationship: Steady RANS tends to overpredict high-speed areas and underpredict wakes against a tunnel; Toronto accepts two-equation RANS or LES; City of London avoids standard k-epsilon. Transient or LES may reduce wake bias.

parameters.name: Mesh and probe height
parameters.relationship: Features under 1 m rarely matter (Toronto), but City of London asks for cells of 0.3 m near entrances and corners, 10 cells across a street canyon and 3 prism layers below 1.5 m. Coarser near-ground mesh -> poorer 1.5 m speeds.

parameters.name: Reference and inflow profile
parameters.relationship: VAF depends on where U_ref is defined: the Eddy3D ABL defaults to 10 m, 5 m/s and z0 1 m with a log law; City of London wants a reference above 100 m clear of the model. Log-law validity at 150-300 m is unverified.

parameters.name: Fidelity level
parameters.relationship: Rules (M03) -> ML surrogate -> RANS -> wind tunnel: reliability for gusts rises, speed falls. Surrogate vendors claim seconds to minutes; independent accuracy for supertall downtown contexts is not verified.

parameters.name: Context scenario
parameters.relationship: Existing plus approved towers change upwind sheltering and channelling; Toronto models projects approved in the last 5 years, City of London consented schemes, Hamilton future cases only if warranted. The VTC brief names future approved towers, so the cumulative case is required.

metrics.name: Directions simulated
metrics.good: At least 16 equal sectors for CFD (Toronto); 36 for tunnel (Toronto, Hamilton) and for any City of London study
metrics.bad: Fewer than 16 for CFD; Hamilton's prevailing-only CFD is accepted by Hamilton but fails Toronto
metrics.method: Check run metadata
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.2 and 6.4.3; Hamilton Technical Requirement 1.A allows prevailing directions for qualitative CFD and 1.B requires 36 for tunnel; City of London 36. The earlier claim that both cities require 16 CFD directions is corrected

metrics.name: Modelled context radius
metrics.good: At least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond it
metrics.bad: 350 m or less, or no upwind towers beyond the radius
metrics.method: Measure from site boundary to the domain context edge; list added towers
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.1: 350 m is a minimum and tall buildings outside it that could influence the site must be included; Hamilton and City of London 400 m; the 2H term is a team assumption

metrics.name: ReferenceSpec on the VAFField
metrics.good: Reference height, z0, profile law and probe height declared; empty-domain run passes
metrics.bad: Reference missing: M04 refuses the field
metrics.method: Schema check plus the empty-domain test of M04
metrics.basis: City of London requires a stated reference; Eddy3D's VAF page names no reference height, so users must copy their ABL settings

metrics.name: Bias-sensitive validation (FAC2, FB, NMSE)
metrics.good: FAC2 at least 0.5, absolute fractional bias at most 0.3, NMSE at most 4 on an AIJ benchmark (editable)
metrics.bad: Outside these bands, or no benchmark run
metrics.method: Compute at benchmark probes; report with hit rate; r only as supplementary
metrics.basis: Bands recalled from air-quality-model evaluation practice (Chang and Hanna 2004), not opened and not a wind-comfort standard; Hagbo and Giljarhus report none of these metrics

metrics.name: Hit rate against reference data (COST 732 / VDI 3783-9 style)
metrics.good: 66% or higher (recalled, to confirm)
metrics.bad: Below 66%
metrics.method: Fraction of probes within stated tolerance of the reference
metrics.basis: Recalled from COST 732/VDI practice; Toronto only cites COST 732 as the guideline to follow; originals not opened

metrics.name: Agreement with wind-tunnel benchmark (Pearson r)
metrics.good: Report r per direction as supplementary information only
metrics.bad: Used as pass/fail: r is scale-invariant and would pass a model that underpredicts speeds by 35%
metrics.method: Correlation of CFD vs tunnel at probes for an AIJ benchmark
metrics.basis: Hagbo and Giljarhus Table 5: r 0.61 (247.5 deg) to 0.84 (180 deg), text says 0.71-0.84; mean speed differences -1% to -35%. The earlier 0.71-0.84 pass/fail band is corrected

metrics.name: Domain and blockage logged
metrics.good: Domain height, lateral and outlet distances in H and the blockage ratio stored in MethodMetadata
metrics.bad: Not logged
metrics.method: Compute from the case files
metrics.basis: Hagbo and Giljarhus used 6 H, 15 H and 15 H; blockage limits in COST 732/AIJ not opened

metrics.bad: Unpinned or silently upgraded
metrics.method: Read the container tag

modules.method: Fidelity ladder. L0: M03 rules. L1: ML surrogate (Eddy3D Wind Predictor, GAN surrogate, Infrared.city API), labelled screening-only. L2: OpenFOAM RANS: massing STL plus context to max(400 m, about 2H) and approved towers; domain scaled to H (Hagbo: 6 H high, 15 H outlet and lateral); ABL inflow with a declared ReferenceSpec; snappyHexMesh with 0.3 m cells near entrances and corners; realizable k-epsilon or k-omega SST; one steady run per sector (16 minimum, 36 preferred); probes at 1.5 m; VAF = U_probe/U_ref on the ReferenceSpec; an empty-domain run checks the reference chain. L3: consultant tunnel study (36 directions, about 50 probes). Validate on an AIJ case with FAC2, FB, NMSE and hit rate. Outputs carry method metadata and an uncertainty tag; M04 reads any VAFField, including imported CSV.

modules.name: Outdoor thermal comfort and rain exposure
modules.effort: M: 6-8 person-days (UTCI engine, clamping and counters, time-base switch, MRT input from the sun/shade module, driving-rain index, category maps)
modules.design_question: In which public spaces and seasons do wind, sun, temperature and rain give acceptable outdoor comfort, and where does tower-induced wind or canopy cover help or hurt?
inputs: WindClimate with concurrent temperature and humidity (time base 'concurrent-30y') or EPW/TMYx (time base 'TMYx'); the choice is stored in MethodMetadata
ProbeWindSeries (mean speed series on the same time base) from M04
Mean radiant temperature series from the sun/shadow module (other packet); fallback ladybug-comfort solar-adjusted MRT, labelled approximate
Hourly precipitation concurrent with wind direction (station record; availability in ECCC hourly files not verified)
CanopyCoverageTable from M03 and M07, zone tags and occupancy hours

parameters.name: Pedestrian-level mean wind speed
parameters.relationship: Higher wind lowers UTCI: relief in heat, added cold stress in cold. This tool feeds mean speed, not GEM (team choice). Calm (GEM under 5 km/h most of the time) in full sun risks poor circulation, so Sitting-class wind is not automatically thermally good.

parameters.name: Mean radiant temperature (sun and shade)
parameters.relationship: Shade from tower, podium or trees lowers Tmrt -> lower UTCI in summer, but also removes winter solar gain. Tmrt minus air temperature must stay within -30 to +70 K for valid UTCI.

parameters.name: Air temperature and humidity
parameters.relationship: UTCI is the equivalent air temperature of a reference environment (50% RH, calm air); valid for air temperature -50 to 50 C and vapour pressure up to 5 kPa.

parameters.name: Wind reference conversion to 10 m
parameters.relationship: UTCI expects 10 m wind; Ladybug docs say 10 m speed is 1.5 times the speed felt at ground (attributed to the original Fiala model, no citation). Unscaled pedestrian speed -> cold stress understated, heat stress overstated.

parameters.name: Activity and clothing assumption
parameters.relationship: UTCI assumes walking at about 2.4 met with adaptive clothing; seated plaza users fall outside the assumption and the docs suggest PET for such cases, so sitting-zone results are less certain.

parameters.name: Time base and concurrency
parameters.relationship: A typical-year file is internally consistent but under-represents storms; a 30-year record keeps temperature, humidity and wind concurrent (Arctic outflow, 1-3 times per winter) but has no concurrent solar. Mixing the two scrambles cold-and-windy hours.

parameters.name: Input clamping and exclusion
parameters.relationship: pythermalcomfort returns NaN below 0.5 or above 17 m/s (the official program accepts up to 30 m/s but documents 17). Clipping sheltered hours to 0.5 m/s and counting storm hours keeps calm zones in the denominator; dropping them biases shares.

parameters.name: Wind-driven rain exposure
parameters.relationship: Rain falling with wind from a sector slants onto frontages facing it; stronger wind and wider windward frontage -> more wetted pedestrian area. Magnitude not quantified; a driving-rain index (ISO 15927-3) is a candidate, not opened.

parameters.name: Weather-protection coverage
parameters.relationship: Continuous deep canopies and covered walkways shelter pedestrians from rain and, per Toronto and Hamilton, deflect downwash at the base. Coverage targets in Vancouver guidance were not opened.

metrics.name: UTCI category
metrics.good: 9 to 26 deg C: no thermal stress
metrics.bad: Above 32 (strong heat stress, up to extreme above 46) or below -13 (strong cold stress, down to extreme below -40)
metrics.method: Classify each hourly UTCI with thresholds 46/38/32/26(28)/9/0/-13/-27/-40; Ladybug splits 26-32 at 28 into slight and moderate heat stress
metrics.basis: Ladybug-comfort default thresholds implementing the Broede et al. scale; scale itself not opened

metrics.name: Input validity
metrics.good: 10 m wind 0.5-17 m/s; air temperature -50 to 50 C; Tr minus Ta -30 to 70 K; RH 0-100%; vapour pressure 0-5 kPa
metrics.bad: Outside range: result is NaN or unrealistic if extrapolated; UTCI can also be non-monotonic in wind speed
metrics.method: Enforce limit_inputs in pythermalcomfort
metrics.basis: pythermalcomfort documentation

metrics.name: Clamping rule and excluded hours
metrics.good: Calm hours clipped to 0.5 m/s; hours above 17 m/s or otherwise out of range counted per probe and shown as a separate class; shares use all occupied hours
metrics.bad: NaN hours silently dropped from the denominator
metrics.method: Counters per probe and season; show valid and excluded hours side by side
metrics.basis: Editable rule built on the documented validity limits; the 0.5 m/s clip is a team choice

metrics.name: Time base declared
metrics.good: Concurrent temperature, humidity and wind from one record, or all variables from one TMYx year; label shown on every map
metrics.bad: Typical-year temperature with a 30-year wind record
metrics.method: Check the time-base tag of every input series
metrics.basis: Design rule; default is TMYx because solar is needed

metrics.name: Share of occupied hours with no thermal stress
metrics.good: At least 50% of occupied hours in 9-26 C (editable placeholder)
metrics.bad: Below 25% of occupied hours (editable placeholder)
metrics.method: Count hours per zone in each UTCI category
metrics.basis: No sourced target; team to set per space type

metrics.name: Ground-to-10 m wind conversion
metrics.good: Documented and justified conversion
metrics.bad: Unscaled pedestrian speed fed into UTCI
metrics.method: Apply 1.5 only as an editable default; show a sensitivity band
metrics.basis: Ladybug doc statement attributed to the Fiala model; pythermalcomfort gives no conversion; not checked against the UTCI primary documentation

metrics.name: Weather-protection coverage
metrics.good: Higher share of retail and transit-plaza frontage under canopy than the baseline scheme
metrics.bad: Lower share than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Canopy footprint along each frontage divided by frontage length
metrics.basis: No sourced target; City of Vancouver weather-protection guidance not opened

metrics.name: Driving-rain exposure
metrics.good: Smaller wetted frontage length than the baseline scheme
metrics.bad: Larger wetted frontage length than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Weight hourly rain by wind direction and frontage orientation, reduced by canopy coverage
metrics.basis: Candidate method ISO 15927-3 not opened; no Vancouver threshold found

modules.method: Choose a time base: B) one TMYx year for all variables (default), or A) concurrent 30-year ECCC/ISD temperature, humidity and wind with Tmrt from the sun/shade module (cold-stress screening, no concurrent solar). Per probe and hour: air temperature and humidity from that base; mean pedestrian wind from M04 converted to the UTCI 10 m convention (editable factor, default 1.5), clipped to 0.5 m/s, excluded above 17 m/s and counted; Tmrt from the sun/shadow module. Compute UTCI with the Broede polynomial via pythermalcomfort with limits on; classify with the 10-threshold scale. Aggregate per zone and season over occupancy hours, excluded hours as their own class. Flag zones where wind moves the category versus a calm baseline. Rain: weight hourly precipitation by wind direction and frontage orientation and compare with canopy coverage.

Calendar heat map (day x hour) for a selected probe coloured by the UTCI scale (-40 to 46 C, diverging blue-white-red)
Stacked bars per zone of hours in each stress category plus a grey 'excluded' segment
Wind-effect arrow chips per zone (helps/hurts)
Plan of frontage lines coloured by driving-rain index (0-1), hatched where canopy coverage exists

modules.design_question: Which design changes reduce wind exceedances most, tried in order of large-scale massing first, then architectural details, then localised screens, and what does each cost the design?

WindRiskField from M03
Geometry change log from Layer 0

parameters.name: Orientation, siting and massing changes
parameters.relationship: Largest area of influence: building shape, height, podium and corner changes alter flow over the whole frontage; Toronto instructs applicants to try these first, before details or screens.

parameters.name: Canopies, recessed entrances, base articulation
parameters.relationship: Local mitigation at entrances and walkways; deep and wrap-around canopies redirect downwash away from ground and add rain cover (M06). Effect is confined to a small area and applied after massing options are exhausted.

parameters.name: Wind screens and landscaping
parameters.relationship: Screens at least 6 ft (about 1.8 m) tall and 20-40% porous diffused corner winds in one RWDI project; Toronto requires written City approval to rely on them, and landscaping must be effective at installation.

parameters.name: Construction phasing
parameters.relationship: Interim phases before later buildings arrive can be windier than the final scheme, so phased projects need separate scenarios.

parameters.name: Significant design changes
parameters.relationship: Changes in building count, orientation, setback, massing, height, tower offset from podium or canopies can alter wind enough to require a new study; any such edit marks results stale.

parameters.name: Significance of a class shift
parameters.relationship: City of London rates a change by class shift: windier by one class but still suitable is moderate adverse; safe becoming unsafe or suitable becoming unsuitable is major adverse. This replaces an undefined 'significant degradation'.

metrics.name: Net effect against existing conditions
metrics.good: Improves existing conditions where possible; no probe worsens by a class
metrics.bad: Major adverse: safe becomes unsafe or suitable becomes unsuitable (City of London); Hamilton: significant degradation, especially of safety
metrics.method: Delta ComfortMap per zone and season rated with the City of London scheme
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 significance tables; Hamilton assessment text

metrics.name: Mitigation order followed
metrics.good: Massing first, architectural details second, localised features third
metrics.bad: Screens or trees used to rescue an unmitigated massing
metrics.method: Check the mitigation scenario history

metrics.name: Significant-change trigger
metrics.good: No change in the Toronto 6.2 list since the last run
metrics.bad: Any listed change marks M04 results stale
metrics.method: Classify each Layer 0 edit against the list
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.2 significant design changes

metrics.name: Wind-screen specification
metrics.good: At least 1.8 m tall and 20-40% porous, confirmed by an M05 or tunnel re-run
metrics.bad: Lower or solid screens, or credit taken without a re-run
metrics.method: Check screen objects in the mitigation scenario and the re-run record
metrics.basis: One RWDI project recommendation (Cambridge MA 2021), not a standard; Toronto requires written City approval to rely on screens

modules.method: Maintain a scenario graph (Existing, Proposed, Mitigation A..n, Phase n). Each edit to Layer 0 is classified against the Toronto significant-change list and marks M04 results stale. For each scenario pair compute per-probe change in class and in exceedance fraction, rate it with the City of London significance scheme, and compute the area of public realm moved into or out of the required class. Rank candidate mitigations by tier (massing, architectural, localised) and by area improved, using results from re-runs rather than assumed effectiveness. The mitigation library stores sourced notes (for example screens at least 1.8 m tall and 20-40% porous, wrap-around corner canopies, podium step-backs) as hypotheses with their source project. Output the order, the deltas and a reason log for the board text.

Delta map: blue where class improves, red where it worsens, with safety-class changes outlined in black and significance class in the legend

parameters.name: Height above ground
parameters.relationship: Wind speed increases with elevation, so terraces higher in the tower meet stronger wind; the brief's vertically distributed public uses raise exposure. A quantified gradient is not given in the opened sources.

modules.method: Select Layer 0 spaces tagged public or amenity above grade. Place probes 1.5 m above the terrace floor on a grid and at corners (City of London lists upper-level terraces and balconies as critical locations). Obtain VAF with ReferenceSpec at those probes from M05 (CFD sampling, or the Eddy3D roof-level ML output when building geometry is supplied). Run the M04 engine with the terrace-specific required class, season of use and the family's safety criterion, and report class and safety. Where a terrace fails, propose screens (height and porosity from the M07 library), enclosure or relocation to a leeward face, and re-run. Add the P10 hand-off note listing the tower height, corner treatment and taper that changed.
visualization: Tower elevation or section with terrace markers coloured by summer and winter class
Per-level table with class, gust margin and confidence badge
Corner-hotspot plan for each terrace with screen suggestions

modules.limits: Prediction at height is the least validated part of this packet; steady RANS and surrogates trained mainly on ground-level probes may not transfer to 150-300 m, and the inflow profile aloft is unverified. Wind tunnel testing is the reference. Structural and facade wind loads are separate (P10). Safety sign-off at height needs a specialist.
modules.human_judgment: Programme decisions (open, seasonal closure, enclose or relocate), occupant safety sign-off, and how much high-level exposure is part of the design experience.

sources.title: Pedestrian Wind Comfort Assessment Using CFD Simulations With Varying Number of Wind Directions
sources.extract: Re-read in r1. OpenFOAM steady RANS on AIJ case E; U_ref at 10 m = 5 m/s, results at 2 m; domain height 6 H_max, outlet and lateral 15 H_max; 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, 4/6/8/10 m/s at 5%, no distress criterion; class agreement by area with 64 directions 79/92/96/99% (4/8/16/32); Table 5 r 0.61-0.84 (text says 0.71-0.84); mean-speed difference -1% to -35%; no FAC2, hit rate or NMSE. Reference list cites Franke 2007 (COST 732), Tominaga 2008 (AIJ), City of London 2019.

sources.publisher: Pancholy et al., University of Canterbury (preprint)

sources.title: Deriving the operational procedure for the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), Brode et al.
sources.extract: UTCI is the air temperature of a reference environment (50% RH, calm, Tmrt = Ta) giving the same physiological response; inputs air temperature, wind, radiation, humidity; thermal stress scale and fast polynomial routines provided. Scale values not in abstract.

flags.claim: The City of Vancouver publishes numeric pedestrian wind-comfort criteria or a mandatory wind-study trigger.
flags.detail: None found. vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, bylaws.vancouver.ca, council.vancouver.ca and rezoning.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 again in r1; the Shape Your City copy of the Higher Buildings Policy returned only a download interstitial. Snippets show only a qualitative Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion and an example rezoning condition. Ask the Rezoning Centre.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy wording: a higher building should not contribute to adverse microclimate effects.
flags.detail: Taken from search snippets of the 2011 and 2018 versions. The 1997 PDF named in the brief and the current 2026 review documents could not be opened. The 1997 policy as amended governs until Council adopts the updated policy (targeted spring 2027); the amendment trail itself is unverified.

flags.claim: Default criteria for Vancouver runs are the Toronto 2022 three-class set (Sitting 10, Standing 15, Walking 20 km/h GEM at 80%; safety gust 90 km/h at 0.1% annual).
flags.detail: Updated in r1 (earlier text merged 'RWDI/Toronto'). Chosen as a Canadian downtown tall-building analog because no Vancouver set was found; Hamilton 2026 (10/14/17/20 km/h, equal or stricter at shared classes), RWDI mph and City Lawson are selectable, each with its own safety criterion. Edits stay visible as team assumptions.

flags.claim: Toronto, Hamilton and City of London trigger rules are used as stand-ins for 'when Vancouver requires a wind study'.
flags.detail: All three place a 244-305 m tower in the highest tier (wind-tunnel evidence). Vancouver practice is unconfirmed; for an ideas competition a CFD-level screening is assumed adequate.

flags.claim: Lawson thresholds and RWDI/Toronto thresholds are interchangeable.
flags.correction: They differ in exceedance basis and speed limits: Lawson-type sets use m/s at 5% of time (City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s on mean and GEM); RWDI/Toronto/Hamilton use GEM in km/h or mph at 20%. Using one speed table with the other exceedance gives wrong classes.
flags.detail: M04 enforces one family per run and shows the basis next to each result.

flags.claim: Airport (YVR) or typical-year EPW wind equals the wind at the downtown site.
flags.correction: Toronto requires 30 years of hourly airport data corrected for terrain and scaled via gradient height to the site; a typical-meteorological-year file is not a 30-year record and under-represents storms.
flags.detail: M01 shows a data-quality badge and logs the correction model.

flags.claim: Early CFD can certify gust-safety compliance of a supertall scheme.
flags.correction: Toronto states CFD struggles with separation, eddies and gusts and is not suited to safety-based issues; wind-tunnel testing is required for high triggers. Steady RANS also showed bias against tunnels.
flags.detail: M05 labels outputs by fidelity level and M04 shows safety results as indicative below L3.

flags.claim: Calmer is always better: a Sitting-class wind condition is automatically good for outdoor use.
flags.correction: Toronto notes GEM under 5 km/h most of the time can cause low air circulation, exhaust build-up and heat in full sun.
flags.detail: M04 raises a low-wind flag and M06 tests the thermal side.

flags.claim: Narrow tower gaps are always windier (simple Venturi rule).
flags.detail: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI describe channelling in narrow gaps, but an idealised steady-RANS study found larger uncomfortable zones at gap = 2x height than at 1x height. The relationship is non-monotonic and unquantified for supertall towers.

flags.claim: Infrared.city and other ML surrogates reach 90%+ accuracy within a minute.
flags.detail: Vendor claim; no method or independent validation opened. Training domain unknown; transfer to 244-305 m towers in dense downtown is unproven.

flags.claim: Eddy3D can be embedded in the open-source web tool.
flags.detail: Docs say it is free for all users but state no source licence, and it needs Rhino 8 on Windows or macOS. Treat it as an external tool whose CSV output is imported, until its licence is confirmed. Its GPL-3.0 OpenFOAM solvers are separate.

flags.claim: A hit rate of 66% or more validates a CFD run (COST 732/VDI practice).
flags.detail: Recalled from memory; Toronto only cites COST 732 as the guideline. Original not opened in r1 either. M05 now lists hit rate beside FAC2, FB and NMSE and does not use it alone.

flags.claim: UTCI wind input equals about 1.5 times the wind felt at ground.
flags.detail: Ladybug documentation attributes the factor to the original Fiala model without citation; pythermalcomfort gives no conversion; the UTCI primary documentation was not opened. Kept as an editable default with a sensitivity band.

flags.claim: Target of at least 50% of occupied hours in the UTCI 'no thermal stress' band; rule weights and cut-offs in the M03 risk index.
flags.detail: No sourced targets. These are editable placeholders and must be recalibrated against M05 runs and project goals.

flags.claim: Claude Code skills or MCP servers exist for CFD, OpenFOAM or urban wind analysis.
flags.detail: The MCP registry and skill catalogue searches returned nothing in round 1 and again in r1. A custom MCP wrapper would have to be built.

flags.claim: RWDI and Toronto share one GEM criteria set of 10/15/20 km/h at 80%.
flags.correction: Treat Toronto 2022 (three classes 10/15/20 km/h), Hamilton 2026 (four classes 10/14/17/20 km/h) and RWDI (four classes 6/8/10/12 mph, about 9.7/12.9/16.1/19.3 km/h) as separate CriteriaSets, each with its own safety criterion.
flags.detail: Toronto Table 3 has no Strolling class; RWDI and Hamilton do, and Hamilton's 14 and 17 km/h differ from RWDI's 8 and 10 mph. Evidence: RWDI Cambridge report (S03), Toronto Table 3 (S01), Hamilton Table 1 (S02), re-read in r1.

flags.claim: Toronto and Hamilton both require at least 16 CFD wind directions.
flags.correction: The 16-direction CFD minimum is a Toronto 6.4.2 requirement. Hamilton's qualitative CFD may simulate only the prevailing directions (assessment still weights all directions) and Hamilton requires 36 directions only for tunnel tests; City of London asks for 36 in all studies.
flags.detail: Hamilton Technical Requirements 1.A and 1.B (S02), Toronto 6.4.2 (S01), City of London general requirements (S43).

flags.claim: Steady RANS in Hagbo and Giljarhus achieved Pearson r of 0.71-0.84, so 0.71 is the lower end and r can serve as pass/fail.
flags.correction: Table 5 lists r down to 0.61 (247.5 degrees) up to 0.84 (180 degrees); the 0.71-0.84 range comes from the text only. r is scale-invariant and cannot detect the -1% to -35% mean-speed bias the same paper reports, so it is supplementary only.
flags.detail: Frontiers 2022, Table 5 and validation text, re-read in r1 (S06). M05 now uses FAC2, FB, NMSE and hit rate.

flags.claim: Butterfly is a viable Python API for an OpenFOAM (Foundation v12) pipeline.
flags.correction: Butterfly is unmaintained: latest commits 11 Sep 2020; the only OpenFOAM compatibility commit seen targets ESI OF1706+. Build case templates directly for the pinned Foundation version or use Eddy3D-generated cases.
flags.detail: GitHub commit history opened in r1 (S16). Foundation v13 also exists (S47), so v12 is pinned deliberately for Eddy3D compatibility.

flags.claim: The Lawson criteria in Hagbo and Giljarhus are a verified mean/GEM criteria set.
flags.correction: The paper uses 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, with no distress or safety criterion. The verified primary Lawson-type set in this packet is the City of London 2019 City Lawson (mean and GEM, 2.5/4/6/8 m/s at 5%, safety 15 m/s at 0.022%).
flags.detail: Hagbo and Giljarhus Table 4 and discussion (S06); City of London 2019 (S43). The Hagbo set is kept as comfort-only and unverified lineage; safety output is blocked for it.

flags.claim: RWDI considers sidewalks to need strolling or better.
flags.correction: RWDI says conditions comfortable for walking or strolling are appropriate for sidewalks. Sidewalk requirement: Walking, with Strolling as a preference where the set has that class.
flags.detail: RWDI Cambridge report, section 5.1 (S03); Toronto Table 3 also maps sidewalks to Walking (S01).

flags.claim: A modelled context radius of about 350 m is adequate for this tower.
flags.correction: Toronto states 350 m is a minimum and that tall buildings outside it that could influence the site must be included; Hamilton and City of London use 400 m. For H = 244-305 m, 350-400 m is about 1.1-1.6 H and the brief names approved towers of similar height. Use at least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond.
flags.detail: Toronto 6.4.1 (S01), Hamilton 1 (S02), City of London CFD requirements (S43). The 2H term is a team assumption.

flags.claim: Minimum context radius max(400 m, about 2H), with approved and future towers as a mandatory cumulative scenario.
flags.detail: The 350 m and 400 m minima are sourced; the 2H term and the mandatory cumulative case are editable team choices justified by the VTC context. COST 732 and AIJ domain rules were not opened to confirm.

flags.claim: Imported VAF data (Eddy3D, tunnel, consultant CSV) share one normalisation reference.
flags.detail: They do not necessarily. The Eddy3D VAF page names no reference height; its ABL component defaults to Zref 10 m, 5 m/s and z0 1 m; City of London uses a reference above 100 m; Hagbo normalise at 10 m. M04 therefore requires a ReferenceSpec on every VAFField and refuses to classify on a mismatch.

flags.claim: ECCC hourly station speeds can be treated as hourly mean winds, and Vancouver Harbour CS provides a usable downtown cross-check.
flags.detail: ECCC states speeds are 1-, 2- or 10-minute means ending at the observation; no sourced conversion factor was found. Vancouver Harbour CS appears in the ECCC station list (hourly year options 1976-2026) but wind sensor presence, hourly coverage and exposure were not verified.

flags.claim: Winter and spring storm winds set the worst comfort class in Vancouver.
flags.detail: The statement came from Ontario practice. Vancouver's strong winds are described as Pacific storms and winter outflow, but no seasonal wind-rose source was opened. M04 derives the governing season from the M01 wind rose instead.

flags.claim: M04 stays core as an importer and classifier; core users get M01-M03 plus M04 only when a VAF file is imported.
flags.detail: Resolves the core-versus-v1 conflict with M05 (hosted OpenFOAM is not feasible before 30 Nov). The UI states that without a VAFField only M03 screening is shown. An Eddy3D workflow guide and import template are the minimal VAF path.

flags.claim: UTCI runs by default on a TMYx time base; calm hours are clipped to 0.5 m/s and hours above 17 m/s are excluded and counted.
flags.detail: TMYx keeps temperature, humidity, solar and wind internally consistent. The 30-year concurrent option has no concurrent solar and is used for cold-stress screening. The clipping rule is a team choice built on the pythermalcomfort limits (S12); excluded hours stay in the denominator.

flags.claim: Weather-protection coverage and wind-driven rain exposure can be judged against Vancouver guidance.
flags.detail: City of Vancouver weather-protection guidance and any rain thresholds could not be opened; ISO 15927-3 driving-rain index not opened. M06 reports relative comparison against the baseline scheme only.

flags.claim: CFD acceptance bands FAC2 at least 0.5, absolute FB at most 0.3, NMSE at most 4.
flags.detail: Recalled from air-quality-model evaluation practice (Chang and Hanna 2004), not opened and not a wind-comfort standard. Editable placeholders until COST 732, VDI 3783-9 or AIJ texts are read.

flags.claim: The Hamilton guideline is an adopted City document.
flags.detail: Text says 'last updated February 20, 2026' but the file name ends 'ph1proposed'; the text also says 'four-season basis' while listing two seasons. Adoption status and the season definition should be confirmed with Hamilton staff.

unresolved_relationships: Quantified reduction of pedestrian-level GEM per metre of tower-to-podium step-back, podium height or canopy depth (direction sourced, magnitude not).
Gap-to-height ratio that minimises channelling between adjacent supertall towers (Venturi versus buffeting); only idealised low-rise RANS results seen.

Dominant strong-wind directions and speeds at the downtown Vancouver site compared with Vancouver International Airport and ECCC Vancouver Harbour CS, including Burrard Inlet channelling and winter outflow; needs ECCC or site data.
Percentage speed reduction from chamfered, rounded, stepped or re-entrant corners on a 244-305 m tower.

General effectiveness of wind screens, canopies and trees beyond the single RWDI project (screens at least 1.8 m tall, 20-40% porous), including winter versus summer foliage and 'City in Nature' planting.

How Vancouver staff and the Urban Design Panel judge 'adverse microclimate effects' under the Higher Buildings Policy (no numeric rule found); City of London defines significance by class shift, but Vancouver has no equivalent found.
Correct conversion between pedestrian-level (1.5 m) speed and the 10 m wind input of UTCI.
Effect of neighbouring approved or future towers (named in the brief) on wind at the site, and how a Vancouver review would define the cumulative scenario.
Accuracy of ML surrogates and steady RANS for 244-305 m towers, and for terraces at height; no validation found.
Effect of corner treatment, taper and tower height on structural wind loads and vortex shedding; deferred to P10 (confirm the current Vancouver Building By-law edition first).
Conversion between ECCC 1-, 2- or 10-minute mean speeds and the hourly means the criteria assume; no sourced factor found.

Transfer from open-terrain airport 10 m wind to the downtown reference (z0, displacement height, gradient height): City of London uses ESDU 01008; applicability to Vancouver and Burrard Inlet exposure is unverified.
Validity of a log-law inflow profile above about 100 m for 244-305 m towers and for terraces at 150-300 m.

notes: Key finding unchanged: no City of Vancouver numeric pedestrian wind-comfort criteria or mandatory trigger could be found or opened (vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca and council domains return HTTP 403; the Shape Your City copy of the Higher Buildings Policy gave only a download page). The Higher Buildings Policy (1997, amended; review draft policies due fall 2026-winter 2027, adoption targeted spring 2027) carries a qualitative microclimate criterion seen only in snippets. The packet therefore uses opened analogs: Toronto 2022 (three classes 10/15/20 km/h GEM at 80%, gust 90 km/h at 0.1%, High trigger over 100 m downtown), Hamilton Feb 2026 (four classes 10/14/17/20 km/h, tunnel at 44 m or more, adoption status unconfirmed), RWDI (6/8/10/12 mph) and City of London 2019 (City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s on mean and GEM at 5%, safety 15 m/s at 0.022%, reference above 100 m, significance by class shift). These are separate CriteriaSets, never merged; Toronto 2022 is the editable default. r1 additions: every speed chain carries a ReferenceSpec and M04 refuses mismatches; context radius at least max(400 m, about 2H) with approved towers mandatory; M04 is core only as an importer and classifier, with M03 screening as the only output when no VAF file exists; CFD validation uses bias-sensitive metrics (bands unverified); UTCI uses one declared time base, a logged clamping rule and a rain and weather-protection add-on. Every VTC tower height (244-305 m) lands in the highest analog tier. Early-stage prediction remains limited: CFD is weak on gusts and safety, steady RANS is biased against tunnels (-1% to -35% in one benchmark), surrogates are unvalidated for supertall towers. Structural wind (1-in-50-year design pressures) is handled in P10. Open items for the next round: Vancouver policy text, weather-protection guidance, COST 732/VDI 3783-9/AIJ primary texts, UTCI wind-conversion source, ECCC Vancouver Harbour CS wind record.
